ai.description: This slender, arboreal colubrid reaches 2.5m. It is bright green with a reddish-brown tail and a distinct black stripe through each eye. It features a pointed snout and keeled dorsal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Red-Tailed Racer is best distinguished by its vibrant, brick-red tail and a distinct black stripe running horizontally through each eye, contrasting with its green body.
ai.habitat: The Red-Tailed Racer inhabits humid tropical rainforests and dense evergreen canopies, typically found at low to moderate elevations across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Red-Tailed Racer is a highly agile, diurnal snake that frequently hunts arboreally, using its slender body to navigate tree branches with remarkable speed and precision.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gonyosoma oxycephalum* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding occurs seasonally, with egg-laying often reported between late spring and summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: In the Indian subcontinent, *Gonyosoma oxycephalum* is restricted to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, occurring from sea level up to moderate elevations.
